preamble: Vocalization of the voiceless velar fricative [x] to a palatal or central offglide [j]/[ɨ̯] before a dental consonant. The clearest case is Brittonic: Proto-Celtic *-xt- (from PIE *-kt- and *-pt-) became *-xθ- and then -(i)θ, the fricative surviving only as the second element of a diphthong (Proto-Celtic *sextam > Proto-Brythonic *seiθ > Welsh saith 'seven'). Goidelic kept the fricative (Old Irish secht, ocht, nocht). The Western Romance -ct- > -it- yod (factum > feito, fait) is usually reconstructed via a fronted [ç] stage ([faxtu] > [façtu] > [fajto]) and is covered under k_to_j_glide.

examples.note: The *x of *-xt- vocalized to the offglide, while *t spirantized to θ. Compare Old Irish secht, which keeps [x].
Same development after a back vowel; Cornish cognate eth.
Compare Old Irish nocht 'naked', with the fricative preserved.

examples.to: seizh (Old Breton seith, Middle Breton seiz, < Proto-Brythonic *seiθ)
examples.note: The glide is retained in the spelling ei; the following θ later became zh.
